title: Traced AO never darkens the environment diffuse term, only the small flat ambient
description: render_scene.wgsl: base_rgb = direct + ibl + ambient + emissive. `ambient` goes through rt_or_flat_ambient(), which with RT on returns albedo * rt_irradiance_mask, and the kernel writes irradiance = ambient_color * ao + gi (raytrace.rs:1451) — so traced AO multiplies ONLY the flat ambient_color (atmosphere.ambient_tint * AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE_SCALE 0.15 * material ambient knob). Meanwhile diffuse_ibl = kd_ibl * albedo * irradiance_map * occlusion uses resolve_occlusion(uv), the material BAKED occlusion texture, untouched by RT. In any HDRI-lit scene the environment diffuse dominates, so turning RT on barely darkens contact regions and corners. Read from the shader, not yet measured; the furnace test on lane/rt-furnace-oracle (test B) is the measurement. Fix shape: route traced AO into the diffuse IBL term too, or combine traced AO with the baked occlusion factor before diffuse_ibl uses it.
close_reason: Fixed by ED-A (landed 3158b4f2): env joins the GI gather at every depth and substitutes the raster irradiance map in fs_pbr, so traced AO now darkens the environment diffuse term. Furnace corner leg (shaded/open ratio) green; RT-off cross-check green. k3 (lead)

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: CONFIRMED by measurement and by looking, on lane/rt-furnace-oracle. Scene: white albedo-1 floor, white albedo-1 plate hovering 0.6 above it, uniform L=1.0 environment via the new node.bake_environment uniform mode, lights 0, material ambient 0.0, rt_enabled true, assert_rt_dispatched passing. Result: open=0.97266 shaded=0.97362 ratio 1.0010 — zero darkening. A frame dump is flat white with no contact shadow anywhere. Three independent confirmations: (1) arithmetic — irradiance = ambient_color * ao + gi, ambient_color = 0 with the ambient knob at 0 and gi = 0 with no sun casters and no emissives, so traced AO multiplies zero; (2) the earlier toggle version measured rt_on == rt_off == 0.49377 byte-identical; (3) the picture. Also caught and fixed a vacuity trap in the gate itself: the occluder was 0.5 grey against a white floor and the probe under it sees the PLATE, so the gate passed at ratio 0.5077 by reading albedo as shade. Occluder is now albedo-1 white; never reintroduce a colour difference. Gate is written and #[ignore]d against this bead. FIX FORK, needs Peter: (a) physical — put the occluded environment diffuse into the RT irradiance term and have render_scene.wgsl SUBSTITUTE rather than add, mirroring the reflection path's existing discipline. No new texture, occlusion denoises for free on the existing accumulate/atrous path, kernel already samples prefiltered_env at RT_REFL_HIT_ENV_DIFFUSE_ROUGHNESS for reflection hits so the primary surface can do the same. Cost: breaks the approved semantic 'ambient knob at 0 = true black with RT on', since an environment-lit surface would stay lit at knob 0. (b) conservative — dedicated full-res AO texture multiplied into diffuse_ibl alongside resolve_occlusion, preserving the knob. Cost: new texture plus its own history ping-pong and atrous channel, because splitting AO out of the irradiance loses the denoising it currently gets for free. Blocked on the semantic call, not on engineering.

title: glTF TANGENT attribute is dropped at import; normal maps use a derived cotangent frame
description: The importer never reads the glTF TANGENT vertex attribute (no Semantic::Tangents read in gltf_load.rs) and MeshVertex has no tangent slot (position 16, normal 16, uv at 32). render_scene.wgsl resolve_normal therefore builds its TBN with cotangent_frame(n, world_pos, uv_t) from screen-space derivatives. Two consequences. (1) Mirrored-handedness UVs get the wrong bitangent sign - NormalTangentMirrorTest.glb ships 80 verts at TANGENT.w = -1 precisely to test this, and its V Mirror / U Mirror columns cannot be correct. (2) A derived frame is unstable at atlas seams, and this asset is a packed atlas, so every tile edge is a derivative discontinuity: measured raster max luma 47.6 with the normal map wired vs 1.31 with the normal_map wire stripped, a 36x blowout localised to tile rims (the blown bright rim outlines Peter reported). Fix shape: read TANGENT at import, add a tangent+handedness field to MeshVertex, thread it through the mesh vertex ABI and the raster shader, use the supplied frame when present and fall back to cotangent_frame only when the asset has no TANGENT. This is a multi-crate vertex-ABI change touching every mesh primitive and shader, not a patch. Also the prerequisite for the RT normal-map bug filed alongside.

title: RT reflections are normal-map-blind (traced specular uses the vertex normal only)
description: Measured on tests/fixtures/gltf/khronos/NormalTangentMirrorTest.glb with RT + RT Reflections on, env 0.15 / fill 0 / sun 10: the internal refl_raw channel is BIT-IDENTICAL with the normal_map wire bound vs surgically stripped - differing fraction 0.00000, max abs diff 0.0000, both variants lit over the same 0.0897 of the frame. The map never reaches the kernel. Root cause: raytrace.rs fetch_interpolated_normal returns the barycentric-interpolated vertex normal and there is no tangent-space normal-map perturbation anywhere in the RT kernel; RtNormalSource carries no tangent address and no normal-map texture index. Made worse because render_scene.wgsl SUBSTITUTES rt_reflection.rgb for the prefiltered env fetch (never adds), so turning RT Reflections on actively DESTROYS the shape the raster IBL had - a straight regression from raster for every normal-mapped smooth surface. Symptom in app: tiles read as flat/empty with a faint donut and isolated bright specks. Failing gate is written and #[ignore]d against this bead: crates/manifold-renderer/tests/gpu_proofs/rt_normal_tangent_mirror.rs, normal_tangent_mirror_normal_map_reaches_the_traced_reflection. Fix shape: plumb the glTF TANGENT attribute into MeshVertex and RtNormalSource (bindless address + handedness), sample the normal map in-kernel, build the TBN, perturb n before the reflection lobe. Named stopgap alternative: gate the substitution off where a normal map is bound. Blocked on BUG-wfxe (gltf-tangent-attribute-dropped-at-import).

title: Setting ANY param on an imported def node is a silent no-op — card default re-asserted every frame, no diagnostic

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: AUDIT + LOUD MECHANISM landed on lane/node-param-loud (f71c48bc), not on main. Two corrections to the mechanism as filed: (1) the card default is NOT re-asserted every frame — apply_bindings skips a slot whose outer value is unchanged, so the clobber happens ONCE, in apply_binding_defaults inside BoundGraph::new, plus again whenever the card slot moves. A direct graph.set_param on the LIVE graph after build therefore survives (rt_bug318 relied on that without knowing it). (2) the import does not promote every scene-atom param — scene_exposure::SCENE_VOCABULARY_TYPE_IDS is the exact surface (transform_3d, the four materials, light, the three cameras, camera_lens, atmosphere, bake_environment, scene_object, the five mesh modifiers, rotate_3d) and node.render_scene is curated to RENDER_SCENE_STAMPED_PARAMS = rt_enabled, temporal_upscale, rt_reflections. So render_scene.objects is NOT card-owned, which is why every scene-panel/merge write of objects is fine. AUDIT verdicts. Silently broken, both fixed: rt_bug326_fix_gate (set rt_enabled+rt_reflections on the imported render_scene, rendered with an empty manifest — both arms pure raster, ratio assert vacuous) and rt_bug318_import_toggle test 1 (set rt_enabled on the node, so the build-time RT-on state it documents never existed and the consumed-set shrink direction never ran). Both now drive the card manifest via harness::import_rt_manifest; bug326 also asserts the RT kernel dispatched. Fine because it goes through the card: render_import --param (resolves against preset_metadata.params by id and errors on no match), freeze_profile profile_scene (same), bug319 apricot (toggles the live graph, which survives). Fine because no card owns the param: bug237_light_camera_commit_render_proof (SceneStarter.json has zero bindings), scene_viewport_session (hand-built def, no presetMetadata), viewport_p6_demo, scene_setup_p4_heldout_merge + ui_snapshot fixtures + manifold-editing scene.rs/modifiers.rs (all write render_scene.objects, not stamped). Corpus: ten shipped presets bake a card-owned param; all ten are dead residue where the card default is the shipped look, listed in SHADOW_BASELINE with cleanup as BUG-imsu. RECOMMENDATION on the design question: do NOT make the node param win. Six of the ten bake amount 0.0 under a card shipping 1.0, so flipping precedence renders ColorGrade/Dither/EdgeDetect/Glitch/Strobe/VoronoiPrism bypassed. The live half of the class is BUG-cy3g.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: SCOPE NARROWED after merging main (BUG-ji6q, imported scene keeps the values you set). Mirrored defaults no longer plant, so the scene-vocabulary half of this class is closed at the source — the detector skips default_mirrors_node_param bindings rather than reporting a revert that no longer happens. Remaining live class, still silent, still guarded: every AUTHORED default. That is any preset default plus the import curated bindings (env_mode over env_select.selector, ssao_intensity, the sun fan-outs onto envmap.sun_*, env_intensity onto hdri_gain.gain). title: glTF-imported material params silently dropped in instantiate_def (blocks BUG-pt6g end-to-end)
description: Symptom: glTF-imported materials (via assemble_import_graph -> flatten_groups -> PresetRuntime::from_def_with_device) do not respond to param overrides applied post-import to the flattened def -- confirmed on node.pbr_material ambient and node.bake_environment intensity on tests/fixtures/gltf/the_rosetta_stone.glb: mutating def.nodes params after flatten_groups() correctly changes the def (verified via print), but the rendered output is byte-identical across a 0.05->0.9 ambient sweep and a 0.2->3.0 env intensity sweep. Root cause: unknown, suspects narrowed via source instrumentation earlier this session -- graph_loader.rs instantiate_def (or one of its 4 migration passes: migrate_def_type_ids, migrate_scene_object_wires, migrate_gltf_anim_v2, flatten_groups) silently drops SOME node params (confirmed: bake_equirect_envmap intensity reads its primitive-declared default 1.0 regardless of the def override) while others survive fine (mode param on the same node persists correctly) -- the override loop in graph_loader.rs:679-704 looks structurally correct/unconditional on read, so the drop happens somewhere between a correct-looking write and the primitive run() read. Fix shape: instrument/bisect instantiate_def one migration stage at a time (print node.params before/after each) to find which stage clobbers which params. This blocks real-world verification of BUG-pt6g (lighting macros dead on photoscan imports) -- the unlit-routing fix (this session, lane/unlit-default-lit) is structurally correct and unit-tested, but end-to-end on a real GLB is still dark because of this separate bug. Likely the same mechanism as "the binding-replant bug" the team lead flagged as split into its own bead -- confirm and dedupe before starting new work on it.
close_reason: Duplicate of BUG-ji6q (binding default_value replant) — same mechanism, confirmed by the same instrumentation trail. Root-fix slice tracked there.

title: Binding default_value replant clobbers live node.params on every graph rebuild (BUG-303 relapse class)
description: Mechanism (lane-confirmed with instrumentation, 2026-07-30): card-stamped defs (GLB imports via stamp_scene_node_exposures_into, scene_exposure.rs:166-255) give EVERY node param a BindingDef whose default_value is a frozen snapshot of node.params at stamp time. On every graph build, instantiate_def (graph_loader.rs:679-704) correctly writes def node.params onto the live node, then BoundGraph::new -> apply_binding_defaults (param_binding.rs:629-648) unconditionally replants every binding default_value over it. Two copies of one fact, nothing keeps them in sync — any writer touching node.params for a bound target (def edits, migrations, direct macro/mapping writes) is silently reverted at next rebuild. This is the BUG-303 (import values clobbered to primitive defaults) class relapsed; the old fix only synced the copies at stamp time. Fix direction chosen by lead: ROOT (option B) — remove the duplicate source of truth: seed the binding skip-cache from the live graph value instead of replanting default_value. CAUTION: bound_graph.rs binding lifecycle is load-bearing (OilyFluid Speed regression 903deaa8; apply_inner_overrides cache-clear contract) — own slice with full-context review, not a quick lane. Also: dropped/reverted param writes must become loud. Regression test shape: import fixture, mutate a bound param post-stamp, assert it survives a rebuild.
notes: Bisect result (2026-07-30, CPU-only repro: post-assembly def mutation of bake_environment intensity, survives-rebuild check): BROKEN at every testable commit back to 6b02cba0 (2026-07-12, the commit that ADDED the intensity param + card binding) — no introducing commit; defect born with the param. Mechanism older still: bound_graph.rs traces to 652486d9 (shared BoundGraph unification). BUG-303 (import transforms clobbered, fixed 66772e69/995006eb 2026-07-22) diagnosed the same mechanism against a different symptom — confirmed recurring class. Note: the ParamManifest per-frame path (bound.apply) is IMMUNE — live macro sliders are unaffected by this bug; it bites def edits, migrations, and any direct node.params writer.
close_reason: Closed

title: RT shadows collapse to one caster — moving a zero-intensity sun re-shadows all live lights
description: render_scene.wgsl shadow_factor (RT branch, ~line 611) returns the single RT mask (traced along casters[0] dir, render_scene.rs:4062) for EVERY light — so moving a zero-intensity sun re-shadows all live lights (repro: RtLightTestingV2.manifold, RT on, sun intensity 0). Root cause: RT shadow pass supports exactly one caster, applied globally. Fix shape: per-caster traced visibility (up to MAX_SHADOW_CASTING_LIGHTS=4), per-pixel ray direction + max_distance for point/spot casters, shadow_factor indexes the mask by slot like the raster path.

comments.author: glm-4.7 (dispatcher)
comments.text:
Dispatcher read-only mechanism findings (no probes, no code changes). Companion to /tmp/manifold_seam_review.md (K3's dispatch-gate review). Fable to review.

== The discriminator ==

Shadow/AO/GI/reflection are ONE kernel, ONE dispatch, ONE accel binding (render_scene.rs:4240 calls dispatch_shadow_rays once per RT-ready frame; kernel at raytrace.rs ~L840 casts all four ray types from the same origin, same accel, same walk_with_alpha_test). Therefore any dispatch-level failure theory (encoder cache, command-queue ordering, accel coherence) predicts shadow rays die too. They survive. The failure is DOWNSTREAM of accel traversal, INSIDE the kernel — something GI+reflection read that shadow does not.

That thing is `n` — the interpolated vertex normal at the primary-ray hit (raytrace.rs:885):
- GI: cosine_hemisphere(n, ...) (L1007). Bad n -> rays miss upward -> emissive-hit term -> 0. Matches symptom.
- Reflection: reflect(-V, n) (L1078). Bad n -> rays all-miss. Matches symptom.
- Shadow: biases along p.sun_dir, NEVER n (comment L921 "bias along sun_dir ONLY, not n"). Unaffected. Matches symptom.
- AO: also uses n (L969). Bug says AO survives — OPEN THREAD (Peter suggests this may be observation-level: AO is the subtle channel, a uniform darkening reads as "still working" if not specifically probed).

`n` is read via the bindless normal_sources buffer (RtNormalSource.vertex_base_addr = vertex_buffer.gpu_address() + vertex_offset, raytrace.rs:1981).

== Mechanism candidates, ranked ==

M1 (FAVORED) — normal_sources stale/invalid read under no-refit. ensure_normal_sources (raytrace.rs:1925) rewrites the CPU-mapped rt_normal_sources buffer every RT-ready frame (render_scene.rs:3976). No useResource: for this buffer (the comment at types.rs:238 argues the bound accel transitively makes BLAS vertex buffers resident — true for vertex/index data referenced by the accel geometry, but normal_sources is a SEPARATE kernel-read buffer, not referenced by the accel structure itself). The STOPGAP's refit opens its own device.raw_queue().commandBuffer() (raytrace.rs:406) — a fresh command buffer that may act as an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes become unreliable to the trace dispatch.

M2 — general per-dispatch useResource: absence. dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) never calls useResource: or useHeap: anywhere in manifold-gpu (verified: only two hits, both comments). The "no separate useResource needed" comment at raytrace.rs:1844 is correct ONLY for resources referenced by the accel geometry, not for gi_materials/normal_sources/params_buffer/obj_motion/material textures. M1 may be a specific instance of M2.

M3 — material_textures table staleness via encoder-bind-cache-invalidation bug class. Plausible per-channel split but symptom is "refls all-miss" (walk_with_alpha_test returns false), not "wrong-colored" — texture staleness produces wrong colors not traversal miss. Less favored.

REJECTED — dispatch-level / queue-ordering theories. Cannot explain why shadow+AO survive in a shared dispatch.

== Why the STOPGAP works under M1/M2 ==

Not because the refit fixes the accel (accel was fine — shadow rays prove it) but because the refit's fresh command buffer is an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes unreliable. The STOPGAP's correctness depends on a side effect, not the documented refit contract — why it's a stopgap not a fix.

== Fix shape (lead to steer) ==

1. Declare kernel-read buffers on the trace dispatch via useResource: in dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) — root fix, removes the dependence on the refit's side-effect ordering. Usage: .read for inputs, .write for the four output textures.
2. CHEAPER EXPERIMENT FIRST: the encoder already has compute_memory_barrier_buffers() (encoder.rs:635). Try one line — encoder.compute_memory_barrier_buffers() before tracer.dispatch_shadow_rays at render_scene.rs:4240, remove the stopgap, run the static-scene harness. If RT stays alive, the root cause was coherence not resource declaration — smaller fix. If only useResource fixes it, it was declaration. Both valid, different layers.
3. Delete STOPGAP (render_scene.rs:4058-4073 + rt_frames_since_refit field).
4. Stale-comment cleanup: "no separate useResource needed" comments at raytrace.rs:1844 and types.rs:238 must be removed/rewritten — they are now wrong.

== Cheapest confirmation experiment ==

3-action decomposition already in BUG-jddy: if M1/M2 is right, the "GPU refit command" action ALONE (enqueue an empty/no-op command buffer on device.raw_queue() between CPU writes and trace dispatch, no instance-buffer rewrite, no flag flip) should keep RT alive. If it does -> M1/M2 confirmed.

== File:line anchors ==

- render_scene.rs:3976 — ensure_normal_sources call (CPU writes normal_sources incl vertex_base_addr, no barrier)
- render_scene.rs:4190 — CPU writes gi_materials via mapped pointer, no barrier
- render_scene.rs:4058-4073 — STOPGAP forced-refit block
- render_scene.rs:4240 — single dispatch_shadow_rays call (shared dispatch)
- raytrace.rs:375-425 — refit_accel opens its own commandBuffer() (suspected implicit ordering point)
- raytrace.rs:885 — n = fetch_interpolated_normal(normal_sources, ...) [GI/refl depend, shadow does not]
- raytrace.rs:921-931 — shadow bias along sun_dir NOT n [the asymmetry]
- raytrace.rs:1007 — GI uses cosine_hemisphere(n, ...)
- raytrace.rs:1078 — Reflection uses reflect(-V, n)
- raytrace.rs:1844 / types.rs:238 — the now-wrong "no separate useResource needed" comments
- encoder.rs:521-626 — dispatch_compute_with_accel never calls useResource:/useHeap:
- encoder.rs:625 — compute_cache.clear() after accel dispatch [encoder-bind-cache-invalidation neighborhood]
- encoder.rs:635 — existing compute_memory_barrier_buffers() [the cheaper-fix primitive]

== Open threads for Fable ==

1. AO-discrepancy — bug says AO survives but AO uses n. Likely observation-level (Peter: "not knowing what I am looking at — potentially"). One targeted probe settles it.
2. M1 (normal_sources-specific) vs M2 (general missing-useResource) — predict same symptom, M2 is the more general hazard M1 sits inside.
3. useResource vs memoryBarrierWithScope — different layers, both valid; cheaper experiment (barrier first) bisects.

title: BUG-326 — rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes
description:
### BUG-326 (rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes) — RT primary rays miss on imported glb scenes: the depth snapshot holds near-zero values at object pixels, wp reconstruction is garbage, reflections black, AO/shadow degraded
**Status:** OPEN
**Severity:** HIGH — RT reflections unusable on imported hero assets (AMG GT3 renders black with `rt_reflections` on); RT AO/shadows subtly wrong on the same scenes (Peter 2026-07-25: "shadows look odd at times where I would expect AO"). Hand-authored probe scenes pass, which masked this.
**Symptom:** AMG GT3 (`tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb`) with RT on + `rt_reflections` on renders black/textureless (non-black fraction 0.024 vs 0.096 baseline). Originally read as Base traced reflections (R1)'s v1 shading gap; the Raster-parity reflections build landed (`7ad9bd36`) and the render stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL, proving the shading change never reached the image.
**Root cause (proven 2026-07-25, K3 kernel-probe chain):** the reflection block is gated on `obj_id >= 0` from the PRIMARY visibility ray (`crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs` `trace_shadow_rays`). On imported glb scenes that ray misses at (almost) every shaded pixel: `opaque_depth_snapshot` holds near-zero values at object pixels (AMG ≈ 0.0003–0.005, DamagedHelmet ≈ 0.009–0.04 — measured via temporary kernel debug writing `depth_tex.read(gpix,0)` into `out_refl`), while the hand-authored R1 grid scene holds proper standard-z ≈ 0.995 at its probe pixel (verified numerically: on=1.1 = depth 0.995 × LUT weight ≈ 1.1). `world_pos_from_depth` (standard-z inverse, far = `>= 1.0-1e-6`) reconstructs near-plane garbage, the `dist*1e-3`-bounded primary ray stops centimetres out and misses, the block's else writes zeros, and the WGSL substitution (`rt_flags.x`) replaces the specular env with those zeros → black. Every shading-path debug variant (albedo-only, env-only, constant env sample) left the render byte-identical, confining the fault to the depth/wp/primary-ray path, NOT the reflection shading (Raster-parity's env-at-hit term is proven live by `rt_r1_reflection::raster_parity_env_at_hit_adds_env_term` on the hand-authored fixture).
**Unknown (next oracle):** WHY imported scenes write tiny depth while hand-authored scenes write standard-z. Suspects, ranked: (a) the import graph's `camera_lens` node (probes lack it) alters the projection the E2a prepass uses vs what `world_pos_from_depth` assumes; (b) the E2a prepass (`render_scene.rs:3762`, `shadow_pipeline` + camera `view_proj`) emits a different z convention for these scenes; (c) synthesized import camera near/far defaults. Cheapest discriminator: add a `camera_lens` node to the R1 grid scene and re-measure probe-pixel depth — a flip to tiny values convicts the lens.
**Fix shape:** depends on (a)/(b)/(c): honour the actual z convention in `world_pos_from_depth` (if scene-variant-but-legitimate), or make the prepass write standard-z (if the convention is a bug). Plus a gpu-proof that renders an IMPORTED glb through the RT path asserting primary-hit coverage above a threshold, so this class can't hide behind hand-authored fixtures again.
**Exonerated (2026-07-25, Flash-lane experiment matrix on the R1 grid fixture, debug-kernel depth readout):** `camera_lens` (depth identical with/without: on=1.1002 both) and import camera params (tilt 0.3/fov 0.9: on=0.7965 = different geometry at the probe pixel, not corrupted depth). Remaining suspects: an untested split between the gpu-test harness path (works) and the render-import/in-app runtime path (broken) — same scene through both paths is the next discriminator — or import-graph content beyond the camera (env nodes, transmission, object count).
**Lead seam review (2026-07-25, k3 — full text `/tmp/manifold_seam_review.md`):** the ENTIRE static write/read path is exonerated element-by-element: one `view_proj` local feeds prepass (3769), raster (3264), and `inv_view_proj` (3979); prepass consumes the SAME `ObjectDraw.uniforms.model` as the raster (3635 shares by reference); `shadow_depth.wgsl` writes plain `clip.z/clip.w` (no remap); the batch CLEARS to 1.0 (encoder.rs:1326 — stale-texture theory dead); snapshot is single-sample Depth32Float with correct usage; RT dispatch binds it at texture(0) with no slot collision; gltf meshes are 48-byte `MeshVertex` soup so `vcount`/stride match. **Geometric contradiction:** tiny standard-z ⟺ object pixels at z ∈ [1.0003·n, 1.04·n] — a mm-thin shell at the near plane, geometrically incompatible with a correctly-framed raster image of a 4.5 m car under ANY single-view perspective; the import auto-frame near (`min(0.05, front_margin·0.5)`, scene.rs:171) analytically yields d ∈ [0.5, 0.98]. So either (A) the GPU prepass draw diverges from the CPU matrix math at draw time (bindings/pipeline/vertex-pull level), (B) runtime `view_proj`/`model` VALUES are degenerate (invisible statically), or (C) texture identity at dispatch ≠ texture written (no static evidence). **Next oracle (lane-delegated one-shot probe):** CPU-project known points with the runtime matrices AND read back the GPU snapshot at the same pixels in ONE render_import run on DamagedHelmet — CPU≈0.98/GPU≈0.003 convicts the draw level (A); CPU≈GPU≈0.003 moves the bug to import scene assembly (B).
**Edge note:** probes can pass for the wrong reason — a far-garbage wp still lets the primary ray cross real geometry because `max_distance` scales with wp distance. Probe fixtures should assert wp sanity (probe-pixel depth in a stated standard-z band), not only final image values.
**Probe round 2 (2026-07-25 PM, Flash lane `bug326-depth-probe`, env-gated `MANIFOLD_BUG326_PROBE` raw readback, commit `a2373535`):** the tiny-depth measurement DOES NOT REPRODUCE with a trustworthy oracle. Raw `copy_texture_to_buffer` readback of `opaque_depth_snapshot` (no PNG/LUT in the path): DamagedHelmet GPU 0.983 vs CPU-expected 0.986; AMG GT3 GPU 0.765 vs CPU 0.741; temporal_upscale on/off identical; global min/max/mean healthy (AMG 0.606/1.0/0.936). Git history shows NO renderer code landed between the morning's tiny-depth measurement and this probe — so the morning's numbers were almost certainly an ARTIFACT of its readout path (depth written into `out_refl`, read back through the tonemapped PNG LUT — scene-exposure-dependent, and the import scenes carry IBL/env the grid scene lacks). The depth-corruption theory of the black render is thereby DEMOTED; the live question is whether the black-render symptom itself (non-black 0.024 vs 0.096, byte-identical across shading variants) still reproduces — round 3 measures that matrix. If it does, the next instrument is a RAW primary-hit/obj_id coverage counter in `trace_shadow_rays` (never a PNG readout).
notes: EVIDENCE CHALLENGED 2026-07-25 (Opus code review, opposite-space pass). The "near-zero depth on imported scenes" number is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a depth reading. out_refl is only observable through the shaded image (gpu_proofs/rt_r1_reflection.rs reads final-target luminance), and fs_pbr consumes the substituted value as `specular_ibl = prefiltered * (F0*env_brdf.x + env_brdf.y)` (render_scene.wgsl:1541). Every debug value written into out_refl is therefore scaled by that per-pixel split-sum weight. The R1 grid probes weight ~1.1 (ground material metallic 1.0 / roughness 0.01 / albedo 0.8 — the "LUT weight ~1.1" already noted in the R1 handoff); imported dielectric/dark-metal materials weight 0.001-0.05. 0.995 x 1.1 = 1.1 (grid), 0.99 x 0.04 = 0.04 (DamagedHelmet), 0.995 x 0.003 = 0.003 (AMG). The whole 300-3000x "wrong depth" spread is the material weight. Suspects (a) camera_lens, (b) prepass z convention, (c) near/far defaults are aimed at an artifact — do not spend the morning there without first reading the depth snapshot DIRECTLY (readback of opaque_depth_snapshot, or a full-frame constant write into out_refl) rather than through fs_pbr. ALSO: the "raster-parity build left the render BYTE-IDENTICAL" evidence is weak, not proof the change never reached the image. Asset facts (read from tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb, 78 materials, NO metallicRoughness textures — all factors): the largest group is roughness 0.958, and ~half the materials sit above the refl cutoff+band (0.6+0.1), so those pixels take the no-ray above-cutoff branch (raytrace.rs:1067-1070) and never cast a reflection ray at all; the raster-parity change only touched the reflection-ray HIT branch, and on a hero car over a void background most rays that DO cast escape to the env miss branch. Byte-identity is expected either way. THIRD: metallicFactor is 1.0 on ~90% of the AMG materials, so the car is a full metal in fs_pbr — no diffuse term, its entire appearance IS the specular-env fetch RT substitutes. That is why a zero from RT paints this asset literally black while a dielectric test scene would only look dull; it is an amplifier of the fault, not the fault. Related new bug: BUG-88m (substitution domain wider than trace domain — Blend/Mask objects get out_refl=0 by construction).

Gate: rt_bug326_fix_gate (poll-until-lit; final landing required a flake fix — rerun suppression window reads black on the harness fresh target and its length is load-dependent; solo-passing gate failed under full-suite load at fixed frame counts). title: BUG-156 — fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix
description:
### BUG-156 (fluidsim3d-4k-perf-regression-suspect-bug066-fix) — FluidSim3D no longer holds smooth 60FPS at 4K — HIGH, reported by Peter 2026-07-14
**Status:** OPEN — found not fixed 2026-07-14, reported by Peter during live-rig use.

**Symptom** — FluidSim3D used to run smoothly at 60FPS at 4K output resolution; it no longer does. Peter suspects this is a regression from the BUG-066 fix.

**Root cause** — unknown, not investigated this session, but the suspected culprit is well-formed: BUG-066's fix (`eebac94d`, see the closed entry in `docs/archive/BUG_BACKLOG_CLOSED.md`) resized `edge_slope_3d`/`swirl_force_3d`'s (and the other volume nodes') dispatch grids from `div_ceil(8)` (legacy 8×8×8 workgroup) to `div_ceil(4)` against the freeze codegen's actual `@workgroup_size(4,4,4)` for 3D-volume kernels. Correcting the grid size to match the real workgroup was necessary for correctness (forces were only landing in 1/8th of the volume before), but going from an 8³ to a 4³ workgroup at the same volume resolution means 8x more dispatched workgroups per volume kernel — a real, expected throughput cost of the fix, not an incidental one. Whether that 8x is actually what's landing on the frame budget (vs. some other change since, or the 4³ workgroup being genuinely suboptimal occupancy for this GPU) is unverified.

**Fix shape** — profile FluidSim3D at 4K with the profiler (`manifold-profiler`) to confirm the volume-node dispatches (`edge_slope_3d`, `swirl_force_3d`, and any other 3D-volume kernel sized off `VOLUME_WORKGROUP_3D`) are where the frame time went, comparing against a pre-`eebac94d` build if needed to isolate it from unrelated changes since. If confirmed, the fix is not "revert BUG-066" (that reintroduces the top-right-quadrant forces bug) — it's making the corrected dispatch cheap again: a larger workgroup size for the 3D volume kernels (if occupancy/shared-memory allows), or reducing per-workgroup overhead, while keeping the grid sized correctly against whatever workgroup size is actually emitted.

title: BUG-069 — shipping-license-audit
description:
### BUG-069 (shipping-license-audit) — four license problems in shipped components — HIGH at commercialization, latent until then
**Status:** OPEN — PARTIALLY RESOLVED 2026-07-17: madmom beat/downbeat/tempo model arms DELETED (AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY P2, Beat This MIT code+weights verified at fetch). Remaining: madmom CNN onsets (P6), ADTOF (active bake-off — P3 baselines committed), rusty_link, ffmpeg staging.

**Found 2026-07-08 (Fable, audio-analysis design session; full sweep same day — Python
runtime deps read from `requirements.runtime.mac.txt`, all Rust crate licenses swept via
`cargo metadata`, staging script read).** Peter's ruling, verbatim: *"Using for dev only
isn't good enough, what we build is what the users should have"* — every item below is
release-gating for the commercial cut, not optional.

1. **madmom model files — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** (source is BSD; models say "commercial use
   requires contacting Gerhard Widmer"). Shipped via `bpm.py` / `onset_detection.py`.
   Fix in flight: AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY P2 (Beat This, MIT code+weights) + P6 (full
   madmom removal), both with `rg 'madmom'` zero-hit deletion gates.
2. **ADTOF — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** (code + model; we ship the `adtof-pytorch` port, which
   inherits it). Drum stage of the pipeline. **Peter's direction (2026-07-08): do NOT
   email Zehren yet** — replace instead. Full two-stage approach (DSP stem detectors
   now, own trained drum-stem model to compete — trained on demucs-separated permissive
   data, weights ours) is captured in AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY_DESIGN Deferred #1;
   trigger = commercialization v1.0 gate or drum work resuming. Fresh off-the-shelf
   search when work starts (Magenta E-GMD model / Omnizart were the permissive options
   as of 2026-07, both mid).
3. **rusty_link 0.4 — GPL-2.0-or-later** (`crates/manifold-playback/Cargo.toml:17`,
   used by `link_sync.rs`). GPL is viral for a closed-source binary — this is the only
   non-permissive crate in the whole Rust tree. Ableton Link itself is dual-licensed
   and Peter's proprietary Link license is already pending (competitive-steal-pass),
   but that grant covers Link, NOT the community GPL Rust wrapper. Fix (Peter's
   direction 2026-07-08): once the Ableton proprietary Link license lands, write a
   thin clean-room FFI binding over Ableton's official `abl_link` C wrapper (~a day;
   `link_sync.rs` is the only consumer). **Never copy rusty_link source — copying GPL
   code inherits GPL.** Do not reimplement the Link network protocol; the licensed
   library carries it.
4. **Staged ffmpeg is whatever the dev machine has** (`stage_runtime_mac.sh:253–273`
   resolves `command -v ffmpeg` — a Homebrew build, i.e. `--enable-gpl`). Fix: stage a
   deliberate LGPL-configured decode-only ffmpeg build (the sidecar only decodes) and
   pin its source/offer per LGPL. The future app-side FFmpeg door (MEDIA_BACKEND)
   must pin the same constraint.

**Clean (verified 2026-07-08):** torch/torchaudio (BSD-3), numpy (BSD), demucs (MIT),
basic_pitch (Apache-2.0), librosa (ISC), soundfile (BSD), pretty_midi (MIT); every
other Rust crate is permissive (r-efi is MIT-or-Apache-or-LGPL — choose MIT). Minor
watch: the `lameenc.py` shim / LAME (LGPL — fine as subprocess/dylib, patents expired);
demucs htdemucs weight file license (⚠ verify at commercialization review). Datasets
are NOT affected — eval-only, never bundled.

COMMERCIALIZATION_DESIGN's license review must consume this entry wholesale.

title: BUG-050 — ableton-anchor-yankback
description:
### BUG-050 (ableton-anchor-yankback) — Play-from-cursor: Ableton repeatedly snaps back to the gesture beat, then MANIFOLD clock-dragged after retries exhaust — HIGH (live transport; partial fix landed 2026-07-07, rig confirmation owed)
**Status:** PARTIAL

**Found 2026-07-07 by Peter, first L4 run of the ABLETON_TRANSPORT_SYNC wave (checklist
step 1).** Symptom: press play in MANIFOLD; Ableton keeps snapping back to the gesture
position (~once per retry interval); MANIFOLD's playhead holds for a few seconds (the
pending suppression working as designed), then snaps back when retries exhaust and MIDI
clock reasserts. Root defect (proven, fixed): the pending expectation froze its target
beat — the ack was a point match against a position both engines run away from, and
every retransmit re-seeked Ableton back to the stale anchor
(`transport_sync.rs`, fixed by the moving-anchor amendment — design doc deviation 5;
regression: `t5b`/`t7b` red pre-fix, `f8` pins the property). **Still open:** WHY acks
starved across several retries on the real rig — retry queries (`get/is_playing` +
`get/current_song_time`) should have acked by retry 1 even pre-fix, and the harness
cannot reproduce the starvation (its fake acks too fast in every plausible
configuration; see f8's honesty note). Suspects, unranked: real listener/query reply
latency under load; a reply-routing gap only manifesting live; beat-space offset
between MANIFOLD's timeline and Live's song time in Peter's set. **Oracle:** the
`[ABL-SYNC]` info logs added with the fix — gesture/retry/ack/degrade each dump the
observed snapshot (playing/song_time+age/tempo, or UNOBSERVED). One play-from-cursor
on the rig answers it. **Escaped:** ABLETON_TRANSPORT_SYNC wave, P2 stage — the
harness's FakeAbleton was fixture-overfit (instant first listener report, atomic
play+seek apply, prompt query replies); no scenario modeled a starved ack channel.

title: BUG-297 — multi-session-memory-exhaustion-freezes-machine
description:
### BUG-297 (multi-session-memory-exhaustion-freezes-machine) — concurrent Claude Code sessions jetsam the machine; indistinguishable from BUG-290's GPU freeze from the user's seat
**Status:** PARTIAL (logged 2026-07-21; worktree Spotlight exclusion landed 2026-07-21, Opus Workstream 1). Mitigated earlier same session: two stale rust-analyzer instances flagged for kill; analyzer LRU caps landed.

**Worktree Spotlight exclusion — DONE + VERIFIED (2026-07-21, Opus WS1):** the entry's fix-shape (d) is now implemented durably for the worktree vector. `scripts/agent-worktree.py::ensure_spotlight_exclusion()` drops `.metadata_never_index` at the pool root (`.claude/worktrees/`) on every `acquire`, excluding the entire subtree — all six slots, their `target/` dirs, and checkouts — from Spotlight (Apple-documented per-directory-tree exclusion, no sudo). It sits ABOVE `target/` so `cargo clean` never removes it, and is recreated on acquire so it survives the pool dir being deleted/recreated; the marker lives in gitignored space, so the script IS its version-controlled source of truth (no reliance on a manual System-Settings privacy entry that a fresh clone or a forgetful setup would miss). Chosen over the `.cargo/config.toml` `target-dir = "target.noindex"` rename because that needs a repo-wide audit of hardcoded `target/` paths (a Peter decision) and doesn't cover checkouts. **Verification (no sudo):** before the marker, a worktree `target/` `.rlib` resolved content attributes; after dropping it, the whole `.claude/worktrees` tree returns nothing from `mdfind`, and `mds_stores` — which spiked to ~80% CPU / 500MB RSS while it pruned the newly-excluded ~114GB subtree — fell to **0.0% CPU / 157MB RSS** within 30s and stayed there; `memory_pressure` held ~85% free throughout. That mds spike-then-idle is the exclusion being honored (mds did the pruning work, then stopped touching the tree).

**Remains (honest):** (1) the brief's end-to-end proof — memory_pressure logged during a REAL concurrent gate wave — was deliberately NOT manufactured this session: Peter is actively on the machine and it hard-locks under load, so fabricating a heavy wave purely to observe pressure is the wrong risk. The imminent Workstream-2 bug-debt wave (real gates under the serialize constraint) is the natural place to capture it. (2) The Spotlight vector is now fully closed: **Peter confirmed (2026-07-21) the whole repo is already in the System-Settings Spotlight privacy list** — which is why mdfind returned no repo file. That manual entry covers the immediate churn (worktrees AND main-checkout `target/`); the landed `.metadata_never_index` script fix is the durable/portable layer on top — it survives a fresh clone or another machine and doesn't depend on the per-machine privacy entry being re-added. No sudo attribution or fix-shape (d) `.cargo/config.toml` rename is needed while the privacy entry stands; if Peter ever removes it, the worktree pool stays excluded (script) but the main-checkout `target/` would reindex (that vector would then want a durable lever of its own).
**Recurrence 2026-07-21 (evening, Opus-orchestration session):** repeated HARD lockups while an Opus mid-orchestrator ran landing-review loads (full-workspace nextest + repeated `ui-snap` flow runs = Metal GPU renders) concurrently with Peter using the machine. Peter: "has been investigated and attempted to be fixed a few times" — the mitigations to date have NOT held. NEEDS A DEDICATED INVESTIGATION SESSION with the machine instrumented (memory_pressure log + gpuEve/JetsamEvent correlation DURING an orchestration wave, per this entry's and BUG-290's separation protocol) rather than another post-hoc guess. Until fixed, orchestration sessions should treat "Peter is actively using this machine" as a reason to serialize heavy gates (one workspace nextest at a time, no parallel flow sweeps).
**Severity:** HIGH — same "whole macbook locks up" symptom as BUG-290, and it MASKS BUG-290's conviction: a freeze during a test run proves nothing until the two mechanisms are separated.
**Symptom:** `JetsamEvent-2026-07-21-100109.ips` — machine froze while another agent session ran the full landing gate (workspace clippy + deny + nextest) with NO gpu-proofs involved and NO new gpuEvent. Top consumers at jetsam: FOUR rust-analyzer instances (4.56 + 4.09 + 4.04 + 3.08 GB ≈ 16 GB — one per live Claude Code session on this workspace) plus rustc + nextest process trees. Prior art: `JetsamEvent-2026-07-17-184945.ips` fired 9 min after that day's gpuEvent — both mechanisms were live that evening.
**Root cause:** each session's LSP plugin spawns a private rust-analyzer (~3–4.5 GB warm on this workspace); N sessions + one workspace-scale build/test run exceeds RAM, and macOS thrash + jetsam reads as a total lockup. Stale sessions (12–14 h old tmux panes) keep their analyzers resident.

**Instrumented-session findings (2026-07-21, Fable, morning after the 2026-07-20-evening lockups):**
- **The evening lockups left NO JetsamEvent and NO gpuEvent.** Neither convicted mechanism fingerprinted. The kernel DID enter memory pressure 20:46–20:55 (unified log: `killing_idle_process` osr_code 9 × 4, plus `knowledgeconstructiond` per-process kill) — but desktop macOS does not jetsam regular apps; it **thrashes** (compressor + swap saturation), which presents as a total hard lockup with no diagnostic report. That is the working mechanism for the "indistinguishable from BUG-290" freezes. GPU saturation from concurrent `ui-snap` Metal renders stalling WindowServer remains a possible co-mechanism (also reportless when no fault fires).
- **NEW convicted contributor: Spotlight.** `mds_stores_2026-07-21-000154.diag`: mds_stores dirtied **8.6 GB of file-backed writes over 20:57→00:00** — exactly the orchestration-gate window. Spotlight indexing is fully enabled with zero exclusions, and the repo has SIX worktrees each with its own `target/`; every gate build makes Spotlight re-index gigabytes of artifacts (CPU + IO + page-cache pressure on top of the build itself). `rustc` itself held a CPU-resource violation 20:23–21:31.
- The 10:01 JetsamEvent (morning) was `knowledgeconstructiond` hitting its own per-process limit with ~4 GB still free — pressure, not exhaustion; the four rust-analyzers (4.6/4.1/4.0/3.1 GB) are confirmed in its process table.
- `rust-analyzer-2026-07-21-102454.ips` is a codesigning **Launch Constraint Violation** SIGKILL (binary launched from `/private/tmp/*/rust-analyzer`) — unrelated to memory; note 0 analyzers were alive at 11:45 with 8 claude sessions open, so analyzers respawn on demand only.
- **Instrumentation:** an always-on 10 s sampler was installed then REMOVED same day at Peter's request (too intrusive). If a future wave needs the second-by-second record, run it wave-scoped only: the orchestrator starts a loop logging `kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` + `vm.swapusage` + top-12 RSS every 10 s at wave start and kills it at wave end. Nothing is running now.
**Fix shape:** (a) protocol — only the landing session runs `--workspace` gates (already the rule; today's run by a second agent violated it); (b) hygiene — kill rust-analyzer in idle/stale sessions (respawns on demand); (c) structural — investigate capping rust-analyzer memory (`lru.capacity` / `RA_LRU_CAP` env, cache priming off) or sharing/disabling analyzers in worker sessions; (d) **exclude build dirs from Spotlight** — root option: `build.target-dir = "target.noindex"` in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml` (`.noindex` suffix is the reliable modern exclusion; needs a repo-wide audit for hardcoded `target/` paths first — Peter decision), quick option: Peter adds both repo roots to System Settings → Spotlight → Search Privacy; (e) when a freeze occurs, check `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports` for gpuEvent vs JetsamEvent AND the unified log for `memorystatus` kernel lines around the freeze time — thrash leaves NO diagnostic report, so no-report + kernel pressure lines = this bug, not BUG-290.

title: BUG-290 — gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware
description:
### BUG-290 (gpu-proofs-test-binary-faults-gpu-firmware) — a `manifold_renderer` test binary triggered an AGX GPU fault/restart; whole-display freezes on Peter's machine correlate with GPU test runs
**Status:** OPEN, hardening LANDED 2026-07-21 @ `7cacb965` (cross-process flock in `test_device()` kills the concurrent-process trigger class; `sg_blur_dynamic` radius clamped at 2048 kills the wired-garbage watchdog class). Remaining to close: the conviction run — ONE isolated `cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1` with Peter present (freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel still live; clean ⇒ concurrency was the trigger, downgrade + monitor).
**Severity:** HIGH — stage risk by class: a compute dispatch that can fault GPU firmware in a test could do the same from the live app mid-show. Also the likely cause of Peter's "whole screen freezes, machine still alive" reports.
**Symptom:** whole machine (all displays, WindowServer, ghostty/tmux) freezes during GPU test runs, recovers after seconds. Two distinct firmware fault classes on record (both bug_type 284):
- `gpuEvent-manifold_rendere-2026-07-17-184055.ips` — restart_reason 3 **"BIF0 page fault"**, `is_read=true`, address 4398052055936, guilty_dm 3: a kernel READ an unmapped GPU address (OOB read or GPU-side use-after-free). Directly attributed to a `manifold_renderer` test binary.
- `gpuEvent-<unknown>-2026-07-18-133620.ips` — restart_reason 2 **"progress timeout"**, command_buffer_trace_id -1: a dispatch outran the firmware watchdog (runaway/unbounded loop). Process unattributed.
**Root cause:** unknown; two independent classes to convict. Facts established 2026-07-21: `GPU_TEST_LOCK` (`manifold-renderer/src/lib.rs:87` `test_device()`) is a `static` in-process ReentrantMutex — **zero cross-process serialization**, so nextest (process-per-test) or two concurrent agent sessions running GPU work defeat it entirely; concurrent-dispatch pressure is a live trigger hypothesis (Peter observed another agent running nextest around freeze times). Readback paths use `commit_and_wait_completed` (no test callers of `commit_and_wait_scheduled`), so simple drop-before-complete on the readback path is NOT confirmed. Static audit (Codex gpt-5.4-mini pass + Fable verification, 2026-07-21): `wgsl_compute.rs` `evaluate()` (~:2324) dispatches user-supplied WGSL with no host-side bounds guard — the widest OOB surface by class; `separable_gaussian_body.wgsl:94` `sg_blur_dynamic` derives its loop bound from `i32(radius)` **unclamped** (linear branch clamps to 32 at :133) — verified real, but current gpu-proofs exercise only the clamped linear mode; Plasma's `octaves = 3u + u32(cx*2.0)` loop was flagged but is 3–5 iterations for in-range complexity (saturating cast) — weak. No specific kernel convicted yet. Prior art: `agx-0x78-crash` memory, `ui-present-content-gpu-contention`.
**Fix shape:** (1) enforce cross-process GPU test exclusion — OS-level file lock inside `test_device()` alongside `GPU_TEST_LOCK`, and/or hook-deny `nextest` with `gpu-proofs` — kills the concurrency trigger class regardless of which kernel faulted; (2) clamp `sg_blur_dynamic`'s radius like the linear branch; (3) convict with ONE isolated run (`cargo test -p manifold-renderer --features gpu-proofs smoke -- --test-threads=1`, nothing else touching the GPU): freezes-alone ⇒ single bad kernel, clean-alone ⇒ concurrency trigger. Requires Peter present — a successful repro freezes the machine. Until fixed: never run gpu-proofs while performing/recording or while another session may touch the GPU.

title: GI energy scale constants look unphysical — sun bounce 0.08 and second-bounce fold 0.318
description: Two ad-hoc dimmers on the GI path, both suspected wrong, neither measured. (1) raytrace.rs SUN_BOUNCE_INTENSITY_SCALE = 0.08, whose comment says it "folds the diffuse BRDF 1/pi energy normalization" — but 1/pi is 0.318, so the sun bounce is roughly 4x darker than the stated physics. (2) RT_GI_THROUGHPUT_FOLD = 0.318 multiplies the second GI bounce throughput on top of the hit albedo; for cosine-weighted hemisphere sampling of a Lambertian surface the correct throughput multiplier is exactly the albedo (the pi and the cosine cancel in the estimator), so an extra 1/pi makes bounce 2 about 3.1x too dark. Derived by reading raytrace.rs, nothing run. Oracle that settles it: the white furnace test being built on lane/rt-furnace-oracle, extended to a multi-bounce enclosure — a white surface in a uniform field must return the field radiance exactly, and any deficit is the lost energy. Related: RT_GI_MAX_BOUNCES 1 -> 2 was reverted (f5c66be2) and un-reverted (a1f86ea2) overnight with bare auto-generated commit messages and no rationale recorded either way.

title: RT noise gate certifies frozen noise as converged — stability measured, correctness never
description: scripts/rt_noise_gate.py measures ONLY mean and 99.9th-percentile |pixel delta| between consecutive frames of a paused static scene, per RT channel, against committed ceilings, plus a min_signal_level brightness floor that catches a DARK channel only. No spatial noise measure, no reference image, no convergence check — the module docstring says so outright ("NO IMAGE ORACLE"). Freezing any RT randomness drives every gated statistic to ~0 while brightness is unaffected, so it scores green. Not hypothetical: lane/rt-petal-shadow-flicker freezes the shadow cone jitter seed (RT_SHADOW_JITTER_SEED = 0) and both the gate and a new temporal-stability gpu-proof pass, while the soft-shadow penumbra becomes one fixed sample per pixel forever, screen-anchored under camera motion. Same blind spot covers over-blurring and a biased denoiser. Fix shape: pair the stability gate with a correctness oracle (converged brute-force reference vs the shipping path, plus analytic scenes) and make green require both. Keep the stability gate — frame-to-frame calm is still worth protecting, it just cannot be the verdict alone.

title: Live scene-node param edits are reverted by the card binding until save+reload
description: Editing a scene-vocabulary node param live (graph canvas slider, scene panel row, gizmo drag) is silently reverted until the project is saved and reloaded. SetGraphNodeParamCommand writes only the def node param; the card binding that owns that param (stamped by scene_exposure stamp_scene_node_exposures_into for every node.transform_3d / pbr_material / light / camera / the render_scene RT subset) still carries the OLD default, and BoundGraph::new plants it back over the edit at the next chain/generator/viewport rebuild. The repair pass that re-syncs the binding default from the node value (manifold_core::scene_exposure::migrate_scene_exposures, the BUG-303 repair loop) only runs at project load and bundled-preset load, never after a live edit. Now VISIBLE rather than silent: the build paths record ChainError::CardBindingShadowsDefParam (see BUG-1l7f, imported-def param no-op). Fix shape needs Peter: either run the repair pass after a live node-param edit on a scene node AND write the new value into the instance param_values (which moves the card slider under the performer mid-set), or make the graph-canvas/scene-panel row for a card-owned param read-only with driven styling like the wire-driven case already does (viewport_gizmo drag_write already declines on wire-driven params; card-driven is not checked). Not reproduced end to end in the app yet — mechanism proven at value level by node_graph::gltf_import::tests::editing_an_imported_defs_node_param_loses_to_the_card_and_is_reported.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: NARROWED by BUG-ji6q (imported scene keeps the values you set), which landed on main after this was filed. The mechanism named in the description — apply_binding_defaults replanting the frozen stamp default at every rebuild — is FIXED for scene-vocabulary params: stamp_scene_node_exposures_into marks its defaults default_mirrors_node_param, and apply_binding_defaults now skips planting those, so a live node write stands across a rebuild. Do not go looking at apply_binding_defaults. What survives: apply_bindings (the per-frame path) does NOT honour the mirror flag, so the OTHER revert route is still open — apply_inner_param_overrides pushes the def values then clears the LastAppliedCache, and the next apply writes the card list live value unconditionally over the edit. For a mirrored exposure that live value is the stamp-time snapshot unless the performer has moved the slider, so a node edit still loses on any graph_version bump. Re-verify before doing any work: the fix shapes in the original description were written against the build-time replant and may no longer be the right shapes.

Fails at step 12 (ScrollTo), not the drag: query name "param_row.31_fog_density.slider" has no match because the fog node now mints doc id 32, so the row is "param_row.32_fog_density.slider". Confirmed pre-existing and NOT from the BUG-ji6q binding-provenance work: identical failure at origin/main 55c60bd1, at aee6ba6d, and on lane/bug-ji6q-clobber-test. title: Worktree slot dirty/clean sample is unstable (41 paths -> 0, unexplained)
description: agent-worktree.py list and acquire both reported slot-8 as "dirty (41 paths)" at 2026-07-30 ~20:15; three consecutive `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` runs minutes later reported 0, with no stash, no write from the session, and the branch already landed. list then showed IDLE and another agent acquired it. Root cause unknown, evidence gone. Suspects: stale git index in the worktree that git status did not rewrite (lock contention while all 10 slots were sampled in a loop), fsmonitor/untracked-cache staleness, or mtime churn from a concurrent cargo build. Impact: the ring categorises a slot from ONE porcelain sample, so an unstable sample can strand finished slots (reads dirty when clean) or hand out a slot whose dirt is real - it undermines every slot category. Fix shape: determine whether the flap is index-refresh related (sample twice and compare; check core.fsmonitor and untracked-cache config; try `git update-index --refresh` before sampling), then either refresh explicitly before sampling or require two agreeing samples before trusting dirty-or-clean.

title: RT gpu-proofs *_never_stalls_past_20ms timing tests are contention-flaky under the full suite
description: Affected: rt_r1_reflection::rt_reflections_dispatch_never_stalls_past_20ms, rt_p1_region_probe::rt_enable_first_frame_never_stalls_past_20ms, rt_t2b_temporal_wiring::temporal_upscale_toggle_never_stalls_past_20ms, and glb_conformance_sweep (added 2026-07-30). Evidence: six full-suite runs in one evening produced five single-test failures across three test names in two independent lanes that never shared a worktree; every one passes in isolation (timing ones at 1.4-2.5ms against a 30ms ceiling, the sweep in 183s). So it is the suite, not the code. Root cause unknown; suspect ~125 proofs sharing one Metal device in one process, so ceilings and long sweeps are measured under load the real path never sees, and a fixed ceiling floor cannot adapt to it. Cost is what raises this to P2: it forced a re-run on effectively every landing tonight, which trains people to re-run rather than read the gate. Fix shape: take timing samples in an exclusive section, derive ceilings from a same-run baseline dispatch instead of a fixed floor, and give glb_conformance_sweep its own budget or its own test binary.

title: Auto-wired import SSAO group is RT-oblivious — double AO when RT Enabled
description: The GLB importer auto-wires a contact-AO group (ssao_gtao -> bilateral_blur HV -> Multiply mix, gltf_import/scene.rs ~616-660, CINEMATIC_POST D9 pattern) into every import graph. RT Enabled is a runtime toggle on render_scene, but the AO group is static structure: with RT on, screen-space AO multiplies on top of traced AO — double-darkened corners, and it eats multi-bounce GI (it darkened the emissiveTest bleed Peter was evaluating, RAYTRACING_DESIGN.md forbids the pairing). Fix shape: make the auto-wired group RT-aware — bypass (mix amount 0 / passthrough) when rt_enabled && rt_ready on the upstream render_scene, re-engage on raster; mechanism TBD (rt-active signal wire vs binding). Workaround: delete the node or mix amount 0 manually.

title: MetalRoughSpheres renders alternating white/gold spheres (should be uniform gold)
description: Khronos MetalRoughSpheres.glb: main grid spheres alternate white/gold per sphere; reference render is uniform gold base color with only metallic/roughness varying. Persists with RT reflections OFF (screenshots 2026-07-29) so raster/import side, not RT R3. Root cause unknown; suspects: base-color texture UV/texel fetch on import, per-object material assignment on multi-primitive meshes. Fix shape: compare imported base-color texture + UVs against the glTF json for two adjacent spheres.
close_reason: Not a bug — works as authored. MetalRoughSpheres (reworked Khronos version) contains TWO sphere layers by design: front grid base-color grey #CCCCCC with metallic/roughness varying, plus a gold control sphere behind each (y=0 vs y=8 in mesh space, z-offset 3.2 after root transform). The official Khronos screenshot shows exactly this: white/silver front spheres with gold behind. 'Reference is uniform gold' was the OLD 2017 asset; the current file is the rework. The 'alternating white/gold' look is parallax at an oblique camera — the two offset layers interleave in screen space. Proof: render-import --orbit 0 shows two clean parallel planes (one grey, one gold); --orbit 1.5708 front view matches the official screenshot pair-for-pair, labels readable. Texel-level check: every mesh's authored UVs sample 50% gold / 50% grey stripes of the atlas — exactly the two layers, split by vertex-index halves (y=0 half grey, y=8 half gold). Import, UVs, and texture decode are all correct.

title: RT R2 clamp v2: tone-mapped variance clip (HDR bright-to-black streaks)
description: Peter look 2026-07-29 post-BUG-dx6w: much better, but streaks remain on very fast sweeps and extreme bright-to-black transitions. Root cause: variance clip runs in linear HDR space — emissives at intensity 10+ near an edge inflate neighborhood sigma, box widens enough that stale bright history survives over black. Fix (Karis): compute moments and clamp in Reinhard-mapped space t(c)=c/(1+luma(c)), invert after clamp. Same helper (clamp_refl_history), same debug/value-proof surface (rt_r2_clamp.rs expectations recomputed in mapped space).

title: RT R2: specular history neighborhood clamp (sweep-trail ghosting)

Fix: TAA-style neighborhood clamp — clamp reprojected specular history to current-frame 3x3 min/max color box before the blend in accumulate_irradiance (crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs:1819 area). Value-level gpu proof: stale history -> clamped output vs CPU expectation. Then fresh sweep dump for Peter.

title: No per-object cast-shadows control — emissive prop occludes its own paired light

Any asset using a second UV set (classic for baked AO) samples the wrong channel with NO report line, log, or warning — the most silent gap in the audit (BUG-y5w7 coverage audit 2026-07-28). Fix shape: read texCoord per map, either grow MeshVertex (priced/rejected before — see 48-byte ABI comment) or at minimum emit an ImportReport warning when texCoord!=0 is encountered. title: Animation goldens are write-only — no numerical compare against committed PNGs
description: Animation/skinned goldens in tests/fixtures/gltf/goldens are write-only: assert_phase_sequence_distinct (gltf_import/tests.rs) asserts only pairwise-distinct frames and never reads the committed PNGs back, so a wrong-but-moving render passes. Fix shape: reuse check_golden-style numerical compare against the committed goldens after the distinctness asserts; blocked-by-relates BUG-cs6 (skinned renders all-black headless) which must be fixed first or the baselines are black frames.
close_reason: Goldens are read back now: assert_phase_sequence_distinct compares each frame vs committed goldens (mean-abs <= 2.0, glb_conformance units), regen env-gated and skip-compare, missing golden is a hard error. Pairwise distinctness is a 0.01 mean-abs floor (min genuine phase delta 0.032, milk truck wheels) instead of assert_ne!. Negative-proven: wrong golden fails. Landed in merge 7da1cde2.

title: RT shadow/AO self-intersection: open plane reads vis=0 ao=0
description: Found during the pause-washout hunt (2026-07-26, RtLightTesting probe): the open plane center reads vis=0 AND ao=0 in out_sv in ALL states (playing and paused) — the shadow/AO rays from the plane self-intersect despite BUG-309s texel-scale-aware bias. The plane fully self-shadows and self-occludes while objects cast/receive correctly-ish. Present in every state, so it is not the pause bug, but it degrades every RT scene with large flat surfaces and may interact with the 38% primary-ray-miss rate on depth-covered texels (also seen in the probe). Suspects: bias direction (origin biased along sun_dir not the normal — for AO/GI rays starting inside the surface), texel_scale under-estimate at oblique angles, or the primary-ray miss class feeding default-up normals. Fix shape: per-pixel hit-t dump on the plane (same method as BUG-309) then bias/origin fix at the root.
close_reason: No longer reproduces at the correct oracle: new permanent rt-capture mask_half channel (raw pre-denoise out_sv) reads plane center vis=0.995 ao=0.935 playing AND paused on main. The inconclusive recheck was the capture harness decoding Rg16Float masks as Rgba16Float (byte-garbled) — fixed on main. AO half cured by BUG-8p1h normal-biased origins; vis rechecked separately per the bead, also clean.

title: BUG-328 rotation-shadow-swap-raster-during-rotation (Peter, lowe.glb)
description: Symptom (Peter, lowe.glb, 2026-07-25): shadows look raster during model rotation, snap back to RT seconds after the rotation stops. Root cause: unknown. Fix shape: shadow-path debug visibility FIRST (visualize which path serves each frame — raster map vs RT mask vs accumulation fallback), then a real multi-frame repro under continuous rotation. title: rt-shadow-path-swaps-to-raster-during-rotation-slow-snapback
description: Peter in-app 2026-07-25 (worktree build with BUG-326 fix): rotating an imported model (lowe.glb) makes shadows visibly switch to what looks like the raster shadow path during motion, then snap back to RT shadows a few seconds after rotation stops. Peter says pre-existing ("I still have the bug"), i.e. NOT introduced by the BUG-326 branch — but VERIFY that anyway: the branch armed a per-topology rerun; if rotation bumps anything in the topo key it would storm rebuilds (check: topo key = buffer identity + tri count + rebuild_epoch; rotation should change none). Suspects: (a) temporal accumulation reset+reconvergence lag reads as the "snap"; (b) refit-lag: traced shadows follow stale transforms during motion (BUG-320 latch trade) and catch up on stop; (c) BUG-320/322 family residual. Fix shape: first reproduce on main vs branch (split case), then a debug overlay/param showing the active shadow path so the swap is observable instead of guessable. Related: BUG-320, BUG-322, BUG-326.
close_reason: Live-confirmed fixed by Peter 2026-07-28 alongside BUG-7xh4 (same symptom, same session): no raster swap during rotation, no slow snapback. Same cure: Metal memory fix + BUG-320 in-place refit.

title: rt-reflection-substitution-domain-wider-than-trace-domain (blend+mask objects black)
description: Symptom: with RT reflections on, any AlphaMode::Blend object (AMG GT3 has 11 BLEND materials — glass, lenses) shades with ZERO specular IBL and goes black. Root cause: producer/consumer domain mismatch. The E2a opaque-depth prepass and the RT accel are both built from `shadow_caster_draws` (render_scene.rs:3635-3638), which excludes Blend. At a Blend pixel the depth snapshot therefore holds the pass clear value 1.0, the trace kernel takes its void branch (raytrace.rs:814-825) and writes out_refl=(0,0,0,0) — but fs_pbr substitutes rt_reflection for its prefiltered-env fetch for EVERY shaded object (render_scene.wgsl:1531), Blend included. The kernel comment at raytrace.rs:822 states the false assumption: "void background reflects nothing (no fragment shades there either — the raster never reads this texel)". Same gap for AlphaMode::Mask: the depth-only prepass pipeline has a void fragment shader (no alpha test) so it writes depth at masked-away texels, while the RT primary ray DOES alpha-test (walk_with_alpha_test) and skips that triangle — the dist*1e-3-bounded ray then misses, obj_id=-1, out_refl=0, black. Fix shape: the substitution domain must equal the trace domain — either gate the WGSL substitution on a validity channel written by the kernel instead of substituting unconditionally, or include Blend/Mask in the prepass+accel with correct coverage. Found by code review 2026-07-25, reading opposite-space to the BUG-326 depth line.
close_reason: LANDED 13653dd5. Fix: out_refl alpha is now a validity signal (>0 hit, 0 env-miss, -1 no-value); fs_pbr substitutes rt_reflection only on .a >= 0, so Blend fragments (excluded from depth prepass + accel) keep their prefiltered-env IBL. Two-site kernel change + the WGSL gate; the upsample_shadow void branch stomped -1 to 0 and had to carry it (found by red-painting the fallback branch — it was never reached). Gate rt_bug88m_blend_specular_gate: chrome Blend quad (dielectric F0 0.04 too small to discriminate from trace noise), refl on/off diff: pre-fix 10.7% pixels >0.3 HDR, post-fix 0.0000%. Harness lessons: (1) imported defs stamp scene exposures and render(empty manifest) re-asserts stamped params at DEFAULTS every frame — def-level param inserts on imported defs are silently overridden; (2) Opaque AMG body is byte-identical across the refl toggle (raster-parity) so only Blend pixels can discriminate; (3) rt_p1 stall test is a load-flaky timing assert (green solo). Peter in-app look (AMG glass) pending. k3 (lead)

title: BUG-226 — golden-png-tests-overwrite-their-own-references-every-run
description:
### BUG-226 (golden-png-tests-overwrite-their-own-references-every-run) — the animated/skinned/morph gpu-proof "golden" tests regenerate their checked-in reference PNGs unconditionally instead of diff-gating against them — found 2026-07-17, lane/glb-triage (BUG-221 session), by reading the writer code after 16 goldens showed up modified in an unrelated run
**Status:** OPEN — MED (verification infra; a "golden" that rewrites itself on every run gates nothing — a regression in skinned/morph rendering would silently update the reference instead of failing).

**Symptom:** running the animated/skinned/morph gpu-proof tests leaves 16 modified files under `tests/fixtures/gltf/goldens/` (box_animated, cesiumman_skin, fox_skin, animatedmorphcube_morph, morphstresstest_morph) even when rendering is unchanged — and would do the same if rendering were BROKEN.

**Root cause:** the tests' writer path unconditionally writes the rendered PNG to the golden path every run (confirmed by reading the writer code, 2026-07-17); no compare-then-fail branch exists.

**Fix shape:** standard golden pattern — compare against the checked-in reference with a tolerance (the conformance suite's comparator is the precedent), fail on mismatch, regenerate only behind `MANIFOLD_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`; add a meta-check that the goldens dir is clean after a suite run. One mechanical session.
close_reason: Fixed by 249355ec (BUG-324/325 session): golden writes now gated behind MANIFOLD_REBASELINE_GOLDENS=1 and only run after assertions pass; per-run frames go to gitignored target/mesh-snap. Remaining deeper gap (goldens are write-only, never compared) split to a new bead.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: BUG-b6i (dup, closed 2026-07-28) added: a single gpu-proofs run leaves ~24 modified goldens in the tree; combined with BUG-cs6 (skinned proofs render all-black headless), an unnoticed commit would poison the goldens with black frames and make the proofs self-consistent-but-wrong forever. Fix must land diff-gating, not just stop the dirty tree.

### BUG-319 — live forced-output toggles need a real runtime rebuild; in-place recompile retracted
**Status:** OPEN (mitigated 2026-07-23: toggles inert + loud log, no crash, no corruption; RT toggle restored to first-look behavior)
**Severity:** MED (feature gap): `temporal_upscale` (and `rt_enabled`'s stored G-buffer) applied live take effect only after the scene runtime rebuilds (project reload / layer rebuild). Not a crash, not corruption.
**History (one night, recorded so nobody repeats it):** BUG-317 recompiled the plan in place on the forced-outputs epoch — panic fixed, but the app import scene went permanently magenta ("object_0 vertices unwired"). BUG-318 added executor memoized-state invalidation — healed a real `from_def` shrink-direction repro, app unchanged. Three headless repro attempts (synthetic scene_object graph, mixamo GLB both directions, THE actual apricot GLB) all pass on the exact code that fails in-app — the app's registry/preset/panel path diverges somewhere unobserved. The executor's own doc says "plans never swap under a live executor — topology changes rebuild the whole runtime"; it means it.
**Fix shape (design session, not a patch):** treat a forced-outputs change as the topology change it is — signal the HOST to rebuild the runtime (pending_segments-style flag), accept the documented state-loss/rebuild cost (D17-style soft transition). Prerequisite: an app-path repro (flow-driver script: import GLB, toggle RT via the real panel) so the fix is verified against the path that actually breaks. Graph::forced_outputs_epoch plumbing is kept — it is the signal the host fix will consume.

title: BUG-227 — madmom-onset-detector-not-gain-or-timestretch-invariant-on-real-mixes
description:
### BUG-227 (madmom-onset-detector-not-gain-or-timestretch-invariant-on-real-mixes) — the current onset detector (madmom CNN, pre-P2/P6) fails two of the three P1 metamorphic invariant checks on real babyslakh mixes — found 2026-07-17, AUDIO_ANALYSIS_ACCURACY_DESIGN.md P1, by the eval harness's own metamorphic suite (`eval/metamorphic.py`) run against real audio for the first time
**Status:** OPEN — MED (accuracy, not correctness — the pipeline still runs; but it means onset timing/counts are measurably gain- and tempo-sensitive on real polyphonic material, which the P1 gate literally asks the metamorphic suite to rule out and it currently does not).

**Symptom:** `python -m eval.run --set dev` (scoreboard: `tools/audio_analysis/eval/scoreboard/dev_2026-07-17.json`) shows, on 3 babyslakh tracks: `noise_floor_silence` passes cleanly on all 3; `gain_invariance` fails on 2/3 (max matched onset-time shift 80-210ms under ±6dB, well past a 21ms tolerance already loosened once to absorb the detector's own 10ms frame quantization); `time_stretch_invariance` (±5%) fails on all 3 (matched-pair shift 244-250ms, alongside event-count drops of -2 to -12 out of 50-88 base events — i.e. 4-18% of onsets disappear or relocate under a 5% speed change). Diagnosed directly (not inferred): Track00001 goes from 66 detected onsets at normal speed to 54 at +5% speed, with several closely-spaced onset pairs collapsing into one detection.

**Root cause:** the madmom CNN onset activation (100fps, 10ms hop) has real per-onset sensitivity to both absolute level and playback-rate changes on dense polyphonic material — plausibly the peak-picking threshold/combine window interacting with closely-spaced onsets whose relative spacing shifts under time-stretch, or gain shifting which of two nearby candidate peaks wins. Not a harness bug: the two implementation bugs the harness itself had (a noise-floor renormalization step that defeated its own test, and an unbounded nearest-neighbor matcher that force-paired unrelated events into a fake "shift") were found and fixed in the same session — see `eval/metamorphic.py`'s `check_noise_floor_silence` and `_max_matched_time_shift`. What's left after those fixes is the finding above.

**Fix shape:** this is exactly what P4 (Precision post-processing pass, D6: rolling-median adaptive baseline + refractory windows applied to onset activations, non-causally) is designed to fix, and/or what the P2/P6 detector swaps (Beat This, SuperFlux) are expected to improve on incidentally. No action needed before P2 lands — P4's gate should re-run this exact metamorphic suite and treat "gain/time-stretch invariance now green" as evidence the precision pass is working, in addition to its named P/R/F1 gate. Escalate to Peter only if P4 lands and these still fail.

title: BUG-118 — render-scene-fog-washes-out-instead-of-depth-grading
description:
### BUG-118 (render-scene-fog-washes-out-instead-of-depth-grading) — atmosphere fog reads as uniform washout, not distance-graded haze — MED look-quality / render_scene
**Status:** DEFERRED — Peter, 2026-07-14: "I don't want bug-118 worked on." On hold at his call; no session touches it until he revives it. Prior state, kept for that day: root cause CHARACTERIZED by the V6 sweep (2026-07-13, VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN.md P1, numbers below); the shafts design (P1–P3) has now SHIPPED (2026-07-13), but whether it actually resolves this bug's original complaint is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed: P2/P3's own acceptance demos don't produce a visually legible light-driven sculpting effect (see that design's landing report and its status line) — no session has re-rendered the original Apricot Weather macro-scale repro scene with shafts on to confirm the milk-washout symptom is actually gone in practice. Do not mark this FIXED until that re-render happens and someone looks. **Absorbed-by: `docs/VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN.md` (2026-07-13, D4/P1–P3)**.
Verified-open-despite: VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN (shipped, but its acceptance demos never re-rendered the original Apricot Weather repro, and Peter froze this bug 2026-07-14 — the verify+mark step is done: still open by his call).

**Symptom** — `node.atmosphere` fog at even low density (0.04) washes out the whole
frame uniformly: near geometry loses contrast as much as far geometry, so fog reads
as a milk filter instead of depth. Seen live in Apricot Weather (macro scale, camera
distance ~9), 2026-07-11. Stopgap: fog card removed from the preset, density zeroed.

**Root cause (CONFIRMED by V6 measurement, 2026-07-13)** — `apply_fog` IS correctly
distance-scaled (`fog = 1-exp(-density·dist)`, `shaders/render_scene.wgsl:516-526`);
the washout isn't a math bug, it's saturation: the visible depth RANGE across a
bounded subject (a photoscanned plant a few world-units deep, viewed from ~9 units
away) is small relative to fog's characteristic decay length `1/density` (25 units
at density=0.04), so the fog fraction barely changes across the subject's near/far
extent — reading as uniform milk — even though the SAME density differentiates
strongly across a scene with a wide depth range (e.g. a ground plane extending to
the horizon).

Measured via `render-generator-preset` (a temporary scratch preset — grazing-angle
200×200 ground plane, orbit camera, one overhead Sun, `node.atmosphere` at
density 0.04 vs 0.0 — deleted after the sweep, not committed) at camera distances 9
and 30, `--size 640x360 --frames 3`:

| camDistance | wide-range near/far ratio-of-ratios (bottom-of-frame vs near-horizon band) | narrow-band ratio (two adjacent bands near the bottom of frame, ~subject-scale depth) |
|---|---|---|
| 9  | 1.1828 | near=0.9797, far=0.9689 → Δ=0.0108 (1.1%) |
| 30 | 1.2951 | near=0.9355, far=0.9102 → Δ=0.0253 (2.5%) |

The wide-range columns confirm the formula differentiates near vs far when the
depth range is large (far attenuates 15–30% more than near across the full scene).
The narrow-band columns are the diagnostic: across a subject-scale depth slice near
the camera, the attenuation delta is only 1–2.5 percentage points — exactly the
"reads as flat milk" signature Peter saw, and it gets WORSE (not better) at the
farther camDistance=30, because both near and far surfaces are then farther from
the camera (more overall fog) while their relative depth range stays the same.

**Fix shape** — not a fog-curve tweak (rejected, D4): the analytic exponential fog
is correct and stays. The fix is VOLUMETRIC_LIGHT_DESIGN's marched light shafts,
which read the scene per-light rather than as a single constant-color blend —
light-driven inscatter can sculpt depth on a bounded subject where a distance-only
fog curve saturates. P2/P3 land the march; this entry closes when Peter's look-pass
on the P2/P3 acceptance demo confirms the "milk" complaint is resolved.

title: BUG-155 — camera-rotation-params-missing-smooth-360-wrap
description:
### BUG-155 (camera-rotation-params-missing-smooth-360-wrap) — camera orbit/tilt/rotation controls don't smooth-wrap at 360 degrees, so a full rotation can't be modulated cleanly via a saw wave — MED, reported by Peter 2026-07-14
**Status:** OPEN — found not fixed 2026-07-14, reported by Peter during live-rig use.

**Symptom** — the camera orbit, tilt, and rotation params jump/discontinue at their wrap boundary instead of wrapping smoothly through 0/360 degrees. A saw-wave LFO driving a full rotation (the standard way to drive continuous spin from a modulation source) hits the seam and snaps instead of reading as continuous rotation.

**Root cause** — unknown; not investigated.
